xray.one_line: Salesforce's Agentforce: autonomous AI agents that read and act on CRM data across service, sales, marketing and commerce, inside the Einstein Trust Layer.
xray.what_it_does: Agentforce is Salesforce's platform of autonomous AI agents, built into the Salesforce Platform, that answer questions, resolve cases, qualify leads and take actions for customers and employees around the clock. Agents are built from subagents (topics), natural-language instructions and actions made from existing Flows, prompt templates, Apex and APIs, grounded in CRM and Data 360 data, with MuleSoft, MCP and A2A reaching other systems. The Einstein Trust Layer wraps them with dynamic grounding, data masking, zero data retention, toxicity detection and an audit trail. [s1, s2, s3, s9, s12, s7]

situations.title: SalesBleed: a poisoned web lead hijacks the agent (2026)
reach: The Leads table, which anyone on the internet can write to through the unauthenticated Web-to-Lead form; the agent reads it when an employee asks about leads
The Accounts table (company names, deal sizes), readable by the same Query Records tool because the default General CRM subagent holds read access to both Leads and Accounts
Trusted URLs, the redaction layer that strips untrusted URLs from agent output after the agent generates it
The chat surface and Slack, which fetch external image URLs and unfurl links automatically, without a click
Slack threads and channels, through the Reply to a Slack Thread action, posting under the agent's identity
asked_our_example: As reported: the employee asks the agent to check the latest leads and help with the newest one
Read the leads and accounts the employee is working on; post to Slack only with the employee's confirmation and under their name; send nothing to destinations the organization has not trusted
gap: One subagent identity held attacker-writable input (leads), read access to sensitive data (accounts) and an output that renders links and images: the researchers call it a version of the lethal trifecta, and say these are defaults, not misconfigurations.
The only barrier between the agent's output and the outside was redaction applied after generation, and the redactor and the renderer disagreed on what a URL is.
Reply to a Slack Thread posted without user confirmation and without naming the user who invoked it, so the agent could speak in Slack beyond what the employee asked.

situations.title: Service Agent resolving cases, orders and refunds
reach: Cases, customer history and interaction notes
Orders: order inquiries, cancellations, exchanges, returns and refunds
Customers directly, on voice, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger and websites
Unified customer profiles in Data 360, including external data connected by Zero Copy (for example loyalty data held in Databricks)
Flows, Apex, prompt templates and MuleSoft APIs turned into actions that can reach other systems
asked_our_example: Answer questions and resolve cases for the customer in the conversation, using that customer's records only
Cancellations, returns and refunds within the published returns policy; anything outside it goes to a human with a summary
gap: Every Flow, Apex class or MuleSoft API made into an action extends the agent's reach to whatever that automation can touch, which can be wider than the service job.
Refunds and order changes have money consequences, and the policy check depends on data quality: Salesforce's own example shows a 30-day returns rule failing on dates in the wrong format.

situations.title: Banking agent disputing charges and issuing credits
reach: Recent transactions on the customer's account
The customer, in a conversation to identify unauthorized charges
Triggers without a person: changes in data, business rules, automations or API calls from other systems
asked_our_example: Identify disputed charges with the authenticated cardholder and open a dispute
Provisional credits and merchant notices above a set amount wait for a human
gap: Salesforce describes the agent issuing provisional credits and notifying merchants all before a human needs to intervene: money and outside parties are in reach on the agent's own judgement.
Agents can start from data changes or API calls, so a dispute flow can run with no customer or employee in the loop.

questions: The default General CRM subagent reads both Leads, which anyone can write through Web-to-Lead, and Accounts: can an admin split those so an agent reading public leads cannot query accounts, and will that become the default?
User confirmation on Slack write actions is now on by default but can be switched off with one click: is turning it off recorded in the Audit Trail, and can it be alerted on?

Trusted URLs redaction runs after the agent writes its output: is it now applied identically on every surface that renders agent output (chat, Slack, mobile, Experience sites), and can customers see a log of what was redacted?
For actions that move money, such as refunds, quotes or provisional credits, what approval thresholds can a customer set, and is each approval recorded against a named person?
Which identity does a customer-facing Service Agent run as, and can a customer list every record and system an agent can reach through its actions before it goes live?
incidents: 2025-07: ForcedLeak (CVSS 9.4, scored by the researchers): Noma Labs showed that instructions hidden in a Web-to-Lead description field could make Agentforce query CRM lead data and send it in an image request to a Salesforce-allowlisted domain that had expired and been bought for $5. Salesforce re-secured the domain, enforced Trusted URLs for Agentforce and Einstein AI from 8 September 2025, and said it had released patches that prevent output in Agentforce agents from being sent to untrusted URLs. [s15, s16, s17]

2026-06: SalesBleed: Zenity Labs reported three flaws: two bypasses of the Trusted URLs redaction allowing zero-click exfiltration of account data from a poisoned web lead (in chat and through Slack link previews), and a Reply to a Slack Thread action that posted without confirmation or attribution, usable for phishing under the agent's identity. Salesforce fixed all three (confirmed 21 September 2026), said it had no evidence of exploitation, and changed Slack action defaults to require confirmation. [s18, s19, s20, s21]

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of Salesforce's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
